data.title: Local and Remote File Inclusion
data.summary:
The application incorporated user-supplied values into file path operations
without validation, allowing arbitrary files to be read from the server and, in
some configurations, executed.
data.description:
The application selected files to include or display based on a value supplied in
the request. Because the value was neither validated against a fixed set of
permitted options nor constrained to an expected directory, traversal sequences
could be used to reference files elsewhere on the filesystem.

This permits the contents of arbitrary files readable by the application account
to be retrieved, including application source code, configuration files
containing database credentials, and operating system files that disclose user
accounts and service configuration.

Where the referenced file is processed by a server-side interpreter rather than
returned as text, the impact extends to code execution. An attacker who can place
content of their choosing anywhere on the filesystem (through an upload
function, a log file that records request data, or a session store) can then
cause that content to be executed by referencing it through the vulnerable
parameter.

Where the platform permits inclusion of remote resources, an attacker can supply
a URL under their control, causing the application to retrieve and execute
attacker-supplied code directly.
data.impact:
An attacker could retrieve the application's source code and configuration,
including credentials for databases and connected services, and enumerate the
operating system configuration. Where the conditions for execution are present,
this extends to arbitrary code execution on the server, resulting in complete
compromise of the host and a foothold within the internal network.
data.recommendation:
1. Avoid constructing file paths from user-supplied values. Where the request
   must select between files, map the supplied value to a fixed internal
   identifier through an allowlist, and reject anything not present in it.

2. Where a path must be constructed, resolve it to its canonical form and verify
   that the result falls within the intended directory before any file operation
   is performed. Filtering traversal sequences from the input is insufficient, as
   encoding variations defeat it.

3. Disable the inclusion of remote resources in the platform configuration, as it
   is rarely required and converts file inclusion directly into code execution.

4. Restrict the application account's filesystem access so that it can read only
   the directories it requires, limiting what is exposed should the controls
   above fail.

5. Store configuration files containing credentials outside the web root and with
   permissions restricting them to the accounts that require them.
